entities.summary: Chien-Shiung Wu, also known as Madame Wu, was a Chinese-American particle and experimental physicist who made significant contributions in the fields of nuclear and particle physics. Wu worked on the Manhattan Project, where she helped develop the process for separating uranium into uranium-235 and uranium-238 isotopes by gaseous diffusion. She is best known for conducting the Wu experiment, which proved that parity is not conserved. This discovery resulted in her colleagues Tsung-Dao Lee and Chen-Ning Yang winning the 1957 Nobel Prize in Physics, while Wu herself was awarded the inaugural Wolf Prize in Physics in 1978.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Chien-Shiung Wu's discovery that parity is not conserved led to a fundamental shift in our understanding of particle physics, paving the way for major advances in nuclear energy and medicine. Her work also highlighted the importance of women in STEM fields.
